elements.before: Independent, lender-grade analysis for assisted living, memory care, and the seniors housing continuum across HUD-FHA Section 232, SBA, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac Seniors Housing, USDA, and bank and bridge capital. This page is our standing read on where senior housing is supply-constrained and where legacy oversupply lingers, how going-concern lease-up forecasts fail review, and the difference between the market study a lender requires and the feasibility study that surrounds it.
elements.after: Boston senior housing runs at 93.6 percent while parts of the Sun Belt are still absorbing legacy oversupply.1 Feasibility Study Company prepares assisted living and memory care feasibility studies, written for owners, developers and the lenders who carry their debt, in a form HUD Section 232, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac Seniors Housing, SBA, USDA, bank and bridge reviewers can each read. Because a national average says little about one community, each study opens with a market study that sizes demand by penetration and care level, schedules a lease-up a credit officer can test, and carries a going-concern pro forma through debt service. Describe the community and its capital stack to start.

elements.before: Feasibility Study Company prepares independent Assisted Living & Memory Care feasibility and market studies, built to the review standard your capital source applies. A methodology briefing walks through the analytical framework, the deliverable and appraisal basis your capital source requires, and the current occupancy, penetration, and labor data for your metro and submarket.
elements.after: Send the address, the planned or existing mix of assisted living and memory care units, and the program you expect to use. Feasibility Study Company will explain how the market study and the going-concern pro forma would be framed for that lender, and what data the file still lacks.
